Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), which limits but does not contradict this reading.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Grade 3 (rank 3) Skills under Reading and Phonics / Shared Reading: the first is the Term 2 bullet 'Uses the information from a graphical text, e.g., takes part in a walk around the school by following the directions on a map'; the second is the Term 1 bullet 'Reads instructions in the classroom'. They share substantive instructional coherence as functional, act-on-it reading within the same sub-strand: in each the learner extracts directive information from a real-world text and uses it for a classroom or school task. That coherence is pair-specific rather than generic repetition (the statements share almost no wording beyond 'in'/'the' and the LC tag 'reading'). However, the Term 2 statement is not an expansion of the Term 1 capability along a CAPS growth dimension (more letters, longer text, greater independence); it introduces a different text type - a non-continuous graphical text requiring visual-spatial interpretation - so proficiency with classroom instruction reading is complementary to, rather than a demonstrated support for, graphical-text use. Symmetric relatesTo with null direction is therefore the correct complete judgment; buildsTowards is not warranted on this bounded evidence. Material limitation: both endpoints omit 24 source-evidence items and are flagged truncated, and all listed SFIs carry upstream audit/merge/code context that was not resolvable here.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit under the same Grade 2, Term 2, Reading and Phonics, Group Guided Reading sub-strand (same canonical rank 2, same term, so a same-term developmental direction is permitted). The second statement, 'Uses sight words, phonics, contextual and structural analysis decoding skills when reading', names the concrete word-attack repertoire a learner applies; the first, 'Begins to monitor self when reading, both recognition and comprehension', is a metacognitive control skill that depends on having such decoding and comprehension strategies available to notice and repair breakdowns in recognition and meaning. Command of the decoding strategies therefore supports the likelihood of success in beginning to self-monitor, rather than the reverse. judgment.rationale: Both SFIs sit in Grade R, Term 1 (same coordinate rank 0, same Term ancestor), but in different Skill Areas: the first is Emergent Reading / Phonological-Phonemic Awareness ('Distinguishes aurally between different sounds especially at the beginning of own name'), the second is Emergent Writing / Emergent Writing ('Copies known letters in own name to represent writing: copies own name'). They cohere substantively because both use the child's own name as the anchor for early literacy learning, linking aural sound discrimination at the start of the name with visual-motor copying of the letters of that name — complementary emergent reading and writing work on the same personally meaningful text. Direction is within one grade from the earlier Term 2 to the later Term 3, which the curriculum sequencing policy permits. This supports substantive conceptual coherence within emergent writing without asserting dependency, so relatesTo rather than buildsTowards. Both endpoints carry upstream audit/merge context and truncated source evidence (and truncated LC evidence for the second), so finer-grained source detail is unavailable, though the printed statements themselves are complete and unambiguous.
